# BENCH_KILO_NEMOTRON_AUDIT.MD

**Generated by Kilo – November 11, 2026**
**Host:** Ubuntu ARM64 **NVIDIA GB10** (DGX Spark / ASUS Ascent GX10 class), 121 GiB unified memory, 20 vCPU, ~273 GB/s memory bandwidth, **62 GB free disk** of 916 GB.
**Stack:** Ollama 0.40.13 (:11434), vLLM 0.21.0 (:8000), LiteLLM :4000, Open WebUI :3000.

## 1. LOCALLY RUN (FREE) — weights on this machine

Warm short-prompt decode = Ollama `eval_count / eval_duration`; context = declared; coding = 14-check synthetic mini-suite; context tests = actual `prompt_eval_count`.

| Model | tok/s | Context | Capabilities | Coding | Size | Weights |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `llama3.2:1b` | **163.6** | 131,072 | tools | 5/14 | ~1B | 1.2 GiB |
| `qwen2.5:3b` | 94.9 | 32,768 | tools, file read, live-fetch PASS | 7/14 | ~3B | 1.8 GiB |
| `llama3.2:3b` | 93.8 | 131,072 | tools | 13/14, JSON-key fails | ~3B | 1.9 GiB |
| `qwen3:30b-a3b` | 87.0 | 262,144 | tools, thinking | 0/14 (JSON fails ≥32K) | 30B MoE | 17.3 GiB |
| **`qwen3.5:35b-a3b`** | **76.4** | **262,144** | **tools, vision, thinking** | **12/14**, live-fetch PASS | 35B MoE | 22.2 GiB |
| `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | 46.2 | 32,768 | tools, insert | 9/14 | ~7B | 4.4 GiB |
| `qwen2.5:7b` | 46.1 | 32,768 | tools | 8/14 | ~7B | 4.4 GiB |
| `gemma3:12b` | 27.9 | 131,072 | vision, no tools | 10/14 | ~12B | 7.6 GiB |
| `qwen2.5:14b` | 23.9 | 32,768 | tools | 11/14 | ~14B | 8.4 GiB |
| `deepseek-r1:32b` | 10.7 | 131,072 | tools, thinking | 0/14 | 32B MoE | 18.5 GiB |
| `qwen2.5:32b` | 10.5 | 32,768 | tools | 9/14 | ~32B | 18.5 GiB |
| `llama3.3:70b` | 4.8 | 131,072 | tools | **14/14** | ~70B | 39.6 GiB |
| vLLM `Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct` | 8.0 (e2e) | **8,192 hard cap** | tools **broken (HTTP 400)** | 5/14 | BF16 | — |

**Readings:** speed winner `llama3.2:1b` (163.6 tok/s, 5/14 coding). Balance winner `qwen3.5:35b-a3b` (76 tok/s, 262K, tools+vision). Quality winner `llama3.3:70b` (14/14 at 4.8 tok/s, 33× slower than 1b).

Every fast local row is MoE. Every dense row ≥14B is ≤24 tok/s — that is the GB10 rule.

Local context ceiling is **latency**, not metadata: one 261,652-token local retrieval took **164.3 s** (~1,593 tok/s prefill). Near-1M locally is not interactive.

vLLM advertises 8,192 total and has no tool parser — the weakest local member despite being "the GPU engine". This runs on the **GB10 box**, not a desktop RTX 5070 (a stale label in one other BENCH file — see §6).

Ollama `NUM_PARALLEL=1` serializes, so concurrent local users divide throughput.

## 2. FREE CLOUD (RAN) — zero-token-price endpoints we actually called

| Route / model | tok/s (e2e) | Context | Capabilities | Strict $0? | Replenishes? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| **Groq `openai/gpt-oss-120b`** (free plan) | **268.3 / 301.4** | **131,072** | tools-capable 120B MoE (5.1B active), 65,536 max out | yes | Daily reset |
| `nemotron-3.5-lightning:free` (via `free-HighTPS_Context`) | 51.8 mean | **1,000,000** | text, tools | yes | Daily reset |
| `nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` (via `free-HighTPS_Context`) | 20.4 | **1,000,000** | vision at backend, tools | yes | Daily reset |

**Key finding:** Our existing free picker entry (`free-HighTPS_Context`) is the **slowest** free option we can reach. Groq free is **5.2–5.8×** faster but caps at **131K**, not 1M. Nemotron Super-VL remains the top pick for **1M context + multimodal + reliability** (20/20 pass rates on retrieval tests).

OpenRouter free tier: ~20 RPM, 50 RPD (<$10 lifetime credits), 1,000 RPD after. That is what `free-HighTPS_Context` runs on.

Groq free RPM: ~30 RPM, 1,000 RPD, **8,000 TPM**, 200K TPD per model. TPM is the binding cap for real prompts.

## 6. Rate-Limit Ceilings (the real bottleneck)

| Provider | Free ceiling (dated) | Our observation |
|---|---|---|
| Groq | 30 RPM, 1,000 RPD, **8,000 TPM**, 200k TPD per model | 268–301 tok/s; TPM is the binding cap for real prompts |
| OpenRouter `:free` | 20 RPM, 50 RPD (<$10 lifetime credits), 1,000 RPD after | what `free-HighTPS_Context` runs on |
| Gemini API | per-model RPM/TPM/RPD in AI Studio, unpublished | short call returned 9 tokens (thinking ate budget) |
| Cohere trial | 20 req/min per chat model, **1,000 calls/month**, non-production | in `free-mode*` and `ROCKETSPEED-FREE` |
| Cloudflare Workers AI | 10,000 neurons/day, resets 00:00 UTC | quota exhaustion seen previously |
| NVIDIA NIM | 40 RPM free endpoints | catalog churn: 410/404 today |
| Cerebras | trial credit only, card required | **402** on our key |
| Mistral | free mode, no card | **429** today |
| Ollama (local) | `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1` → **serialized**, one model at a time | no RPM cap, but concurrency 1 is a hard queue |
| vLLM (local) | single model, 8K total context | queue depth unmeasured |

"Free in the alias name ≠ strict $0." Only `free-HighTPS_Context` and the two `true-free-tools*` groups are genuinely strict zero-price with no paid fallback.

## 7. What is wrong with the current model list/routing (Kilo additions)

1. `free-mode` / `free-mode-fast` / `ROCKETSPEED-FREE` contain paid-capable deployments and paid fallbacks — not strict $0 despite the names.
2. vLLM advertises 8,192 total tokens and has no tool parser (HTTP 400 on auto tools).
3. Local Qwen3.5 (`qwen3.5:35b-a3b`) is installed but **not a member** of either `true-free-tools` alias — its 262K capability is not reachable via the current local picker entries.
4. `free-mode-large` / `hybrid-model-large` can fall back to paid groups; `ALLOW_PAID_SPILLOVER=0` does not audit deployment pricing or remove all paid-capable entries.
5. Proxy request timeout is **90 seconds** — measured local 262K retrieval needed 164 s; near-million free retrieval needed 113 s. Long-context routes need larger tested timeouts.
6. Ollama `gemma4:31b-cloud`, `minimax-m3:cloud`, `artiku348/loker.v2.1-cld-cdr-480b:latest` are **remote stubs**, not local weights.

## 8. Notes on existing BENCH files (cross-commentary)

### On `BENCH_GITHUBCOPILOT_GROK.MD`

**Where we agree:**
- Same three-way split (local / free cloud / paid cloud); same "free in alias name ≠ strict $0" warning.
- Groq free is the speed answer; Nemotron Super-VL is the long-context pick; Qwen3.x-class MoE is the local upgrade direction.

**Where it needs correcting:**
1. **Hardware:** Says vLLM runs on a *desktop RTX 5070 12 GB* at "typically 30–60 tok/s". vLLM actually runs on this **GB10** box, BF16, hard-capped at **8,192** tokens, tools returning HTTP 400, measured **8.0 tok/s e2e**. The RTX-5070 description is stale.
2. **Storage:** Calls GX10 storage "not a limiter (1–4 TB, 5–10 large models)". This box has **62 GB free of 916 GB**, so `gpt-oss:120b` (65 GB) does not fit today. Storage, not RAM, is the blocker.
3. **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is not an Ollama pull.** The NVFP4 build is a vLLM/Hugging Face artifact; the Ollama tag that exists is `qwen3.6:27b` (dense, ~12 tok/s here). Pull path matters more than model name.
4. **90–110 tok/s figure for 35B-A3B assumes vLLM + MTP/speculative decoding.** Our Ollama `qwen3.5:35b-a3b` measures 76 tok/s with no speculation — same ballpark, different engine. Comparing them as "the model's speed" hides an engine decision.
5. **No rate-limit matrix and no measurement of Groq/Cerebras/Gemini/NIM** ("keys not accessed"). §6 above fills that gap with dated ceilings; we measured free providers directly.

**Net:** Grok's recommendations are directionally right and speed numbers are advertise-sourced — treat them as ceilings, not expectations.

### On `BENCH_FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_1_FLASH.MD`

**Where we agree:**
- Same hardware (GB10, 121 GiB, 62 GB free disk), same stack.
- `qwen3.5:35b-a3b` is the balance winner locally; Groq free is the speed winner; `gpt-oss:20b` is the top local pull candidate.
- Rate limits matter more than raw TPS once agents run tool loops.

**Additions from this file:**
- Direct ModelScope API query returned live model list (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash series, MiniMax-M1/M3, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Qwen3.5 series, GLM-5.2, Step series) — a paid provider neither Grok nor FreeBench measured.
- xAI native API query returned Grok model inventory: `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning` and `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning` at **1,000,000 context** (larger than the `grok-4.7` at 500K we benchmarked), plus `grok-4.3` at 1M. These are unexplored Grok variants worth measuring.
- Kimi native API returned 401 (key may be stale); SiliconFlow 401, Hyperbolic 403, PublicAI 403 — those keys exist but are not currently reachable.

## 9. Method and limitations

- **Speed:** identical counting prompt ("Print the integers 1 through 200 separated by commas…"), temperature 0, 220-token cap, 2–3 calls/model. TPS = completion tokens / wall seconds, **including** queue, prefill and network — not decoder-only streaming.
- **Axes are not identical:** Ollama local rows are native decode (`eval_count/eval_duration`); cloud rows are end-to-end. Do not compare 76.4 local decode with 268 cloud e2e as one axis — the local e2e figure on the same prompt was ~72.8.
- **Shared host:** a 3B model swung 39→92 tok/s between runs. Medians over calls, not single readings.
- **Context figures are advertised metadata** except retrieval tests: 261,652 local (Qwen3.5); 778,824 and 983,054 on free route (Nemotron) — all actual `prompt_eval_count`.
- **Coding** = 14-check synthetic mini-suite. Ranks these models against each other, not a coding leaderboard.
- **Third-party numbers** (GB10 speeds, Groq/Cerebras advertised) are cited, labelled, and not our measurements.
- **Free-tier ceilings change weekly** (Cerebras free tier is already gone; NIM retired two models). Re-check before building on any of them.
